title: I Stopped Answering the Neighborhood App After the Leaf War

parts.text: I raked my leaves onto my tarp and refused to rake Carol's oak too. I am thirty-three, IT, Saturday, back sore, smell of wet leaves like tea. Carol's oak hangs over the fence and she calls it community shade. Community shade is still her tree. She posted in the chat that decent people do both yards. I posted the city code about overhangs, boring, lethal. She left a rake against my door, a prop. I left it back, gently, like a boomerang with manners. Hasan from downstairs brought me a cider because he is the real community. I bagged my leaves. Hers stayed, then a wind did what wind does. She accused me of witchcraft, basically. I muted the chat. My Saturday returned. The oak is pretty. Pretty is not a work order. My tarp has a hole. I duct-taped it. That is my civic duty. Carol said, "Decent people do both yards" I said, "The code does one" Carol's cousin the tow guy waved from a truck, uninvolved. I waved. Leaves are not a towing issue. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink.

social.video_title: I raked my yard and muted the leaf crusade
social.description: Wet-leaf tea smell, a prop rake, city code. Community shade is still her oak. Would you have done both yards?
